correction.text: Puerto Alonso (renamed Porto Acre) and the lands round it on the upper Acre River

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1899-1900: Luis Galvez 'proclaimed the Republic of Acre on July 14, 1899'; the seat was Puerto Alonso (renamed Porto Acre). The page says he imposed his authority on the lands the Treaty of Ayacucho had given Bolivia and gives no area, so the shape is a radius round the seat. It ended on 15 March 1900. Cliopatria has no row.

correction.text: the upper Acre River from Xapuri to Puerto Alonso, taken by Placido de Castro from 6 August 1902

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1902: Placido de Castro began his campaign on 6 August 1902 by seizing the Bolivian depot at Xapuri and then besieged Puerto Alonso; the page gives no area, so the shape is a radius round the upper Acre River. The second republic of November-December 1900 (Orlando Correa Lopes, defeated around Christmas 1900) held no ground the page names and has no keyframe.

correction.text: the whole Acre region: Castro's forces 'had taken the entire region' by 24 January 1903

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1903: Bolivian forces at Puerto Alonso surrendered on 24 January 1903, Castro's forces 'had taken the entire region' and the Third Republic of Acre was proclaimed on 27 January 1903; the Treaty of Petropolis of 17 November 1903 (191,000 km2) gave the territory to Brazil. The region is the state of Acre.

region.text: Puerto Alonso (renamed Porto Acre) and the lands round it on the upper Acre River

ledger.note: 14 July 1899: Luis Galvez proclaims the Republic of Acre at Puerto Alonso. 'Galvez proclaimed the Republic of Acre on July 14, 1899' after a revolt led by Jose de Carvalho on 30 April 1899; Antonio de Sousa Braga had briefly declared himself president before ceding power to Galvez.
14 July 1899: the rebels contest Bolivian rule in Acre (mirror of the Bolivia dossier).

region.text: Puerto Alonso (renamed Porto Acre) and the lands round it on the upper Acre River

ledger.note: 15 March 1900: Brazil ends the first republic. 'On March 15, 1900, a Brazilian war flotilla reached Puerto Alonso, arrested Galvez, and dissolved the Republic of Acre'; the land goes back to Bolivian administration (the researcher's reading: the page says only that Brazil dissolved the republic).

region.text: the upper Acre River from Xapuri to Puerto Alonso, taken by Placido de Castro from 6 August 1902

ledger.note: 6 August 1902: Placido de Castro takes Xapuri. 'At 5 a.m. on August 6, 1902, Castro led 33 riflemen in canoes on the Acre River' and took the Bolivian depot at Xapuri; he then besieged Puerto Alonso. The extent of ground held is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the whole Acre region: Castro's forces 'had taken the entire region' by 24 January 1903

ledger.note: 24-27 January 1903: Acre is in rebel hands. Bolivian forces at Puerto Alonso surrendered on 24 January 1903, Castro's forces 'had taken the entire region' and 'on January 27, the Third Republic of Acre was proclaimed'.
17 November 1903: the Treaty of Petropolis ends the contest. It 'gave Brazil the territory of Acre (191,000 km2)'.

region.text: the whole Acre region: Castro's forces 'had taken the entire region' by 24 January 1903

ledger.note: 17 November 1903: the republic is absorbed into Brazil. The Third Republic is not said to end formally; the Treaty of Petropolis of 17 November 1903 gave Brazil the territory, a federal law approved it on 25 February 1904, a decree of 7 April 1904 incorporated Acre and Placido de Castro became the first president of the Acre Territory.

wars.name: Acre War

zones.text: the whole Acre region: Castro's forces 'had taken the entire region' by 24 January 1903

wars.outcome: Brazil won: the rebel republics were dissolved (1900), defeated (December 1900) or absorbed (1903) and the Treaty of Petropolis of 17 November 1903 gave Acre to Brazil.
wars.note: Three republics: Galvez (14 July 1899 - 15 March 1900), Orlando Correa Lopes's expedition (November - Christmas 1900) and Placido de Castro's (27 January 1903).

certainty.note: No frontier: the rebels held the upper Acre River and, in 1903, 'the entire region'; the page gives no area.

sources.title: Acre War
sources.note: Republic of Acre proclaimed 14 July 1899; ended by a Brazilian flotilla 15 March 1900; second republic November-December 1900; Castro from 6 August 1902; Puerto Alonso surrenders 24 January 1903; Third Republic 27 January 1903; Petropolis 17 November 1903; decree 7 April 1904.

notes:
Rebel state Cliopatria lacks: three short republics against Bolivian rule in Acre, 1899-1903. One page (Acre War) plus the Treaty of Petropolis page opened. The page does not give the area held by any of the republics, so the keyframes are radii round the places it names (Puerto Alonso, Xapuri), centred on Rio Branco because the gazetteer lacks Porto Acre and Xapuri. The second republic (November-Christmas 1900) held no named ground and has no keyframe. The page's 'Independent State of Acre' is not used. Wikipedia and Wikidata ids are null: no article for the state was opened.
Counterpart strings: bolivia, brazilian-republic. Gazetteer names needed: Porto Acre, Xapuri (places).
